purposePerFile.CanonicalMarketCallbackSurface.t.sol: Standalone (no forge-std inheritance) unit tests for CanonicalMarketCallback (src/market/CanonicalMarket.sol), the abstract before/afterSwap logic that authenticates the canonical USDG/HKMN pool, computes the 3% (300bps) fee on the executed USDG leg, defers fee collection to afterSwap, and credits only the hookData-authenticated recipient with HKMN output. Exercises all four swap quadrants (zeroForOne x exactIn/exactOut) x both token orders (USDG as currency0 or currency1) = 8 combinations, rounding at the fee floor, partial-fill rejection, foreign-pool/foreign-manager rejection, reentrancy fencing, and full PoolManager-routed buys via two harnesses: LocalCanonicalMarketHook (pure unit-level, deterministic 0x00CC-masked address, hand-rolled Vm.prank) and SettlementCanonicalMarketHook (deployed via CREATE2 salt search against a real PoolManager/PoolSwapTest/PoolModifyLiquidityTest).
purposePerFile.FeeAccounting.t.sol: Standalone unit tests (no forge-std) for FeeAccounting (src/accounting/FeeAccounting.sol), the liability-ledger mixin: 3%/10bps/40bps/remainder split math, per-beneficiary programmable/treasury claimable liabilities that freeze at accrual time (treasury rotation does not rewrite past epochs), a single 'moneyPath' lock shared by collection+accrual, payout liability funding/paying, process-fund release, and full adversarial-token-behavior coverage (false return, revert, malformed return, short/excess source or destination delta, reentrancy) verified via state-digest equality (no state change on any failed path) and an explicit isSolvent()/hookUsdgBalance()>=totalLiability() check after every mutating call.
purposePerFile.FeeAccountingInvariant.t.sol: forge-std StdInvariant stateful-fuzz harness wrapping FeeAccountingHarness. Handler exposes accrue/claimProgrammable/claimTreasury/fundPayout/payPayout/releaseProcess/attemptFailedTransition as fuzz targets across 4 treasuries and 4 payout holders. Three invariants: total liability equals the sum of all known per-beneficiary liabilities, token balance always covers total liability (and isSolvent() holds), and no failed money-path call ever mutates the state digest.
purposePerFile.HookemonHook.t.sol: Full forge-std Test.sol integration suite for the concrete HookemonHook contract deployed via CREATE2 (address-mask search for 0x00CC) against a real PoolManager/PoolSwapTest/PoolModifyLiquidityTest, wired to a real PegCycleVault. Covers: exact hook permission bitmap, CREATE2 address-mask enforcement at construction, vault/USDG mismatch rejection, rejection of every unused v4 callback (with distinct selectors for foreign-manager vs used-but-unauthorized calls), all 4 swap quadrants across both token orders with exact 10/40/250bps liability deltas, malformed-ERC20-return handling on collection, and the end-to-end fixed-claims + PegCycle process-release path (claimProgrammable, claimTreasury, openPegCycle) including rejection on every adversarial USDG transfer-return shape for claims, process release, and payout funding.
purposePerFile.PhaseOneLocalLoop.t.sol: A single end-to-end 'Phase 1' local-loop test (no forge-std) that: sets chainid=4663 (Robinhood Chain), verifies HookemonIssuance's official-issuance guard (prepareOfficialIssuance/verifyIssuance) against a hardcoded 420.69B-token supply plan (90%/10% market/remainder split), performs one authenticated buy via hand-pranked beforeSwap/afterSwap on a fake PoolManager stub, shells out via vm.ffi to a Node adapter script to obtain a signed Merkle payout leaf, then funds and pays exactly one PegCycleVault cycle/payout end to end, asserting full conservation (funded==paid, vault/operations end with zero USDG) and isSolvent(). Explicitly documented (line 70) as calling no real provider.
purposePerFile.PhaseOneReleaseInvariant.t.sol: The largest and most comprehensive invariant suite: a StdInvariant-style (hand-rolled targetContract/targetSelector, no forge-std inheritance) stateful fuzzer whose handler wires together FeeAccountingHarness, ProcessBudgetHarness, PayoutCommitmentHarness, a PegCycleVault, a PermanentPositionCustody guarding a MockPositionManager NFT, and unauthorized/replay-attempt callers. 9 invariant_ functions plus 1 plain test (test_releasePlanIsReadOnlyAndRejectsAnAccountWithoutRuntimeCode) that CREATE2-deploys a vault fixture and drives script/release/PhaseOneReleasePlan.sol's validate()/verifyDeployedRuntime() through both accepted and rejected (wrong address, overlapping roles, wrong runtime codehash, empty-account) plan variants.

invariantsEnforced: Total fee is always exactly executedUsdg*300/10000, computed on the executed (post-fill) USDG leg, never the requested/specified amount, and only after afterSwap confirms the finalized delta matches beforeSwap's expectation (CanonicalMarketCallbackSurface.t.sol, HookemonHook.t.sol).

programmable+treasury+process == total for every quote, including quote=0 and quote=type(uint256).max (FeeAccounting.t.sol:10-30, independently re-derived with a rounding-safe _bps helper at line 607-609 and cross-checked against the hardcoded extreme-value literals - verified correct by independent recomputation).

programmableLiability/treasuryLiability are per-beneficiary and freeze at accrual time; rotating the treasury beneficiary does not retroactively change already-accrued liabilities, and a historical treasury can still claim its own frozen epoch after rotation (FeeAccounting.t.sol:44-63,160-207).
isSolvent()/hookUsdgBalance()>=totalLiability() holds after every single mutating call in every test and throughout both stateful fuzz suites.

Every money-moving call (_collectFee, claims, payouts, process release) is atomic: any adversarial ERC20 return shape (false, empty, malformed, short/excess source or destination, reentrant) leaves token balances AND liability accounting byte-for-byte identical (verified via keccak256 state-digest equality, not just individual field checks).

Only the hookData-authenticated recipient (bound via a versioned domain separator HOOKEMON_CANONICAL_SWAP_R54_A3_V1 + operationId + sender + recipient) is credited with HKMN output; the settlement recipient passed to the router is independently checked against it and mismatches revert with InvalidSettlementContext.

Hook address must satisfy the exact 0x00CC/0x3FFF permission mask (beforeSwap+afterSwap+both ReturnDelta flags only); construction reverts otherwise (HookemonHook.t.sol testConstructorRejectsWrongAddressPermissionMask).

Nonzero PoolManager protocol fee on the canonical pool causes the whole swap to revert with no state mutation (CanonicalMarketCallbackSurface.t.sol testPoolManagerRejectsNonzeroProtocolFeeWithoutMutation).

PegCycle authorizations are single-use: cycleId/payoutId/returnReceiptDigest replay is rejected and does not mutate vault state (PhaseOneReleaseInvariant invariant_cycleAndPayoutReplayCannotMutateState, attemptUnauthorizedOrReplay/attemptProductionPayoutViolation).
Operations (the trigger EOA) never custodies PegCycle USDG directly - only the vault/hook does (invariant_operationsNeverReceivesPegCycleUsdG; also explicitly asserted in HookemonHook.t.sol:492,502).

LP-position custody is permanent: no caller other than the custody contract itself can transfer/approve/decreaseLiquidity the guarded NFT (invariant_positionCustodyRemainsPermanent / attemptCustodyControl).
stateTransitions: CanonicalMarketCallback: beforeSwap computes/reserves the fee delta on the specified leg (deferred, not yet collected) -> afterSwap recomputes executedUsdg from the actual finalized delta, calls _collectFee then _accrueAuthenticatedSwap, and credits buyerHkmnCredit for the authenticated recipient only if HKMN is the unspecified/output leg.

FeeAccounting.moneyPath: collect USDG into custody -> _splitLiability -> credit programmable/treasury/process ledgers atomically inside one lock; claims and releases debit exactly one ledger and call _transferExactUsdg, reverting (with full rollback) unless the token confirms an exact canonical `true` boolean return and exact balance delta.

PegCycleVault lifecycle: (unbound) -> authorizeFunding -> openPegCycle (debits process liability, moves USDG hook->vault) -> executeOutbound (vault->route executor, pinned outboundActionDigest+amount) -> off-chain/route return (route executor -> vault) -> authorizePayout -> fundPayoutFromPegCycle (vault->hook, credits payoutLiability, lifecycle becomes RETURNED, commits the payout binding) -> payEntitlement/payPayout debits payoutLiability to the end holder via a Merkle-proved leaf.

HookemonIssuance guard: UNVERIFIED -> prepareOfficialIssuance(plan) records planDigest -> verifyIssuance(plan,observation,trace) checks token metadata/balances/allocation trace against the digest -> OBSERVATION_VERIFIED_PROVIDER_BINDING_PENDING (Phase 1 stops here; provider/launchpad binding is a later, not-yet-tested state).

testStatus: All 6 files compile as ordinary forge test contracts (no forge-std inheritance is required for discovery; forge finds test/invariant_-prefixed functions by name). None of the 6 files contain skip markers, vm.skip, or commented-out assertions - every assertion appears live and unconditional. Execution-gate status differs sharply by file, established by grepping .github/workflows/v4-gates.yml, scripts/verify-phase1-release.mjs, and docs/modules/*.md: (1) test/market/CanonicalMarketCallbackSurface.t.sol IS run in CI via `forge test --match-path 'test/market/*.t.sol'` (v4-gates.yml:169). (2) test/integration/PhaseOneLocalLoop.t.sol and test/invariant/PhaseOneReleaseInvariant.t.sol ARE run, but only by the separate manual/local gate script scripts/verify-phase1-release.mjs (lines 1061-1084), which explicitly passes --ffi plus HOOKEMON_NODE_BINARY for the former; this script is NOT invoked anywhere inside .github/workflows/v4-gates.yml. (3) test/accounting/FeeAccounting.t.sol and test/integration/HookemonHook.t.sol are NOT referenced by name or by directory glob in either the CI workflow or verify-phase1-release.mjs's six expectedChecks; they are documented only as manual developer commands in docs/modules/fee-accounting.md:43-44 (`forge test --match-path 'test/accounting/*.t.sol'` / `test/integration/HookemonHook.t.sol`). (4) test/accounting/FeeAccountingInvariant.t.sol is likewise not referenced anywhere by path; it requires forge's invariant/StdInvariant runner and its 3 invariants are a strict subset of (and are effectively superseded/duplicated by) the same-named invariants inside PhaseOneReleaseInvariant.t.sol's much larger handler, which IS gated. Net effect: of the ~68 test functions across these 6 files, the ones actually enforced by an automated or documented-repeatable gate are the 20 in CanonicalMarketCallbackSurface.t.sol (CI) and the 11 across PhaseOneLocalLoop.t.sol+PhaseOneReleaseInvariant.t.sol (manual release script); the 24 FeeAccounting.t.sol tests, the 10 HookemonHook.t.sol tests, and FeeAccountingInvariant.t.sol's 3 invariants have no CI/gate enforcement recorded, only a documented manual command for two of them.
autonomyGaps: No test in this unit models a real Collector Crypt pack-buy/open/sell(buyback) provider round trip; PhaseOneLocalLoop.t.sol is explicitly self-documented (line 70) as calling no provider, and its route executor (LocalLoopRouteExecutor/ReleasePayoutRouteExecutor) is a `require()`-only stub that always returns the exact pinned amount - there is no coverage for slippage, partial provider fills, provider timeouts, or a failed/foreign buyback.

Every PegCycle open/execute/fund/pay step in every file is driven by an explicit `vm.prank(OPERATIONS)` or an authorized signer contract calling a single named function once; there is no test of an unattended scheduler firing this every N minutes, of overlapping/concurrent cycles, or of a 'stuck cycle' being restarted/kicked - matching the stated fact that Phase 2 automation/dashboard is out of scope here.

FundingAuthorization/PayoutAuthorization carry an `expiresAt` field but no reviewed test exercises the expiry-revert path (an authorization used after expiresAt), which the dashboard's 'restart/kick a stuck cycle' feature would need to reason about.

PermanentPositionCustody (guarding the canonical LP position) is only ever tested against MockPositionManager, a bespoke stub with hand-written ownerOf/liquidity/approve/decreaseLiquidity/mint semantics - none of these tests exercise the real Uniswap v4 PositionManager contract that Robinhood Chain bindings point to (0x58daec3116aae6D93017bAAea7749052E8a04fA7).

The mandatory Programmable-launchpad fee policy referenced for this project states fees must revert below 1000 quote units; no test in any of these 6 files asserts a revert threshold at all - CanonicalMarketCallbackSurface.t.sol's own rounding tests (testMinimumUnitRoundingCollectsOnlyAtFirstFloorUnit, lines 569-574) and fuzz test (testFuzzValidSpecifiedAmountsDoNotOverflow, lines 736-748, exercising amount as low as 1) both show the code silently floors the fee to zero for small trades rather than reverting. Also, none of these tests assert the programmable-liability beneficiary equals the skill-mandated fixed owner address 0x4957f49620AFf3Adbbe8195a4f633E49cc93376c - the 'programmable' beneficiary is always an arbitrary constructor-supplied address (ClaimActor / PROGRAMMABLE=0x5000) in every test file.

No dashboard-facing read surface (status/health, per-cycle history, pack-selection config, interval config) is exercised anywhere in this test unit; the only externally observable state is the low-level liability/lifecycle accessors used directly by the harnesses.

suspicions.note: VM.ffi(command) is called with no `ffi = true` set in packages/contracts/foundry.toml (verified: file has no such key) and CI (.github/workflows/v4-gates.yml) never runs this test path at all. The only place this test is actually invoked is scripts/verify-phase1-release.mjs:1065-1071, which passes --ffi explicitly, and docs/modules/release-evidence.md:49, which documents the same flag by hand. Anyone running a bare `forge test` (or `forge test --match-path 'test/integration/*'`) without --ffi will get this single test failing/reverting with FFI disabled, which could be mistaken for an environment or adapter-script bug rather than a missing flag.

LocalLoopPoolManager, the PoolManager stand-in for the flagship 'Phase 1 local loop' release-gated test, implements only extsload()->0 and nothing else; the 'authenticated buy' (lines 251-256) is not a real PoolManager.swap() call at all - it is a hand-pranked beforeSwap/afterSwap invocation where the BalanceDelta (toBalanceDelta(-9_700,8_000)) is hand-picked by the test author, not produced by executing a swap. Unlike CanonicalMarketCallbackSurface.t.sol and HookemonHook.t.sol (which route real swaps through a genuine PoolManager+PoolSwapTest), this release-evidence test only proves the hook's internal bookkeeping given an assumed delta, not that a real swap produces that delta.

requirementsRevision is hardcoded to the literal 56 here and at line 153, and again in test/invariant/PhaseOneReleaseInvariant.t.sol:685 and :725, whereas test/integration/HookemonHook.t.sol:629 and :658 read it dynamically via vault.REQUIREMENTS_REVISION(). Confirmed today src/process/PegCycleVault.sol:20 defines REQUIREMENTS_REVISION=56, so all four hardcoded sites currently agree - but if this constant is ever bumped (the repository's own Phase 2 branch is already named 'requirements revision 57' per the established facts), PhaseOneLocalLoop.t.sol and PhaseOneReleaseInvariant.t.sol would start failing every authorizeFunding/authorizePayout call with a stale-revision revert, while HookemonHook.t.sol would keep passing silently - a landmine specifically for the Phase 2 migration the owner is asking for.

This file's three invariants (aggregate liability, solvency, rollback-only-on-failure) are word-for-word duplicated (same names, same handler pattern) inside test/invariant/PhaseOneReleaseInvariant.t.sol's much larger handler, which the manual release-verification script DOES invoke by path. This standalone file is never referenced by path anywhere (not in CI, not in verify-phase1-release.mjs, not in any docs/modules/*.md command found), so it is effectively an orphaned/redundant target unless a developer runs `forge test --match-path 'test/accounting/*.t.sol'` by hand - the same command that also silently runs the (also ungated) FeeAccounting.t.sol.

_assertSolvent asserts both isSolvent() and hookUsdgBalance()>=totalLiability(); isSolvent() itself is only exercised through this same helper in every test, so no test ever independently checks a case where isSolvent() and the direct balance/liability comparison could disagree (e.g., an off-by-one in _isSolvent()'s own implementation) - they are always asserted together, so a bug that changes both consistently could pass unnoticed. Low severity given the raw hookUsdgBalance()>=totalLiability() check is done as well, but worth a reviewer's second look at _isSolvent()'s src implementation directly.

CI's two forge test invocations restrict to test/bindings/*.t.sol and test/market/*.t.sol only. Every other test directory in packages/contracts/test (accounting, integration, invariant, process, payout, blind) is untouched by GitHub Actions; the only other automated-ish coverage is the standalone Node script scripts/verify-phase1-release.mjs, which is not wired into any workflow file found in .github/workflows/ (only v4-gates.yml exists).

openQuestions: Should FeeAccounting.t.sol, FeeAccountingInvariant.t.sol and HookemonHook.t.sol be added to .github/workflows/v4-gates.yml (or to scripts/verify-phase1-release.mjs's expectedChecks) given they are the primary tests proving the exact 10/40/250bps fee split, adversarial-token safety, and the full claim/PegCycle integration path that the owner's autonomous-cycle design depends on? Right now they run only if a developer manually types the command documented in docs/modules/fee-accounting.md.

Is the discrepancy between these tests (fees silently floor to zero below the rounding threshold, no revert) and the mandatory Programmable fee-policy requirement (revert below 1000 quote units, per the programmable-v4-hook-builder skill referenced in the task brief) intentional - i.e., does HookemonHook's actual deployed configuration apply a separate, additional 1000-unit minimum-quote guard somewhere outside this test unit's scope (e.g., in the launchpad/router layer), or is this a genuine compliance gap against the mandatory policy?

Is PegCycleVault.REQUIREMENTS_REVISION intended to be bumped to 57 as part of merging the deferred Phase 2 line (codex/phase2-revision-57)? If so, PhaseOneLocalLoop.t.sol:120,153 and PhaseOneReleaseInvariant.t.sol:685,725 will need to switch from the hardcoded literal 56 to a dynamic vault.REQUIREMENTS_REVISION() read (as HookemonHook.t.sol already does) or be updated in lockstep, or every gated release-evidence test will start failing.

Does any test outside this unit (e.g., test/process, test/payout, test/bindings, test/blind, or the JS test-js/runner suites) provide the missing real-PositionManager or real-provider-round-trip coverage that this unit's tests explicitly stub out, or is that coverage genuinely absent repository-wide today?

Why do three of the six files (CanonicalMarketCallbackSurface.t.sol, FeeAccounting.t.sol, PhaseOneLocalLoop.t.sol) deliberately avoid forge-std inheritance and hand-roll their own minimal Vm interface, while the other three use forge-std's Test/StdInvariant - is this a stopgap around the CI Foundry-version-string bug/vendoring issue already documented in the established facts (PR #1/#2 CI failures), meant to be unified once that's fixed?
